Shot November 8 and 9, 2026! 🍁🫶🏻

Where each photo was taken:
• El Capitan Meadow, the reflection shots
• Valley View, the classic river bend
• Cook’s Meadow, golden trees with Half Dome
• Tunnel View, the whole valley in one frame
• Swinging Bridge, the quiet river spot
• The Valley Loop road, golden canopy the whole drive

Hikes:
• Lower Yosemite Fall Trail, 1 mile, easy
• Mist Trail to the Vernal Fall footbridge, 1.6 miles
• Upper Yosemite Fall Trail, 7.2 miles, the big climb
• Sentinel Dome and Taft Point, 2.2 miles each, only while Glacier Point Road is open

Things to do:
• Sunset at Tunnel View
• Bike the Valley Loop road
• Stargazing, the November nights are long
• Mariposa Grove of Giant Sequoias, 45 minutes south

Roads:
• Glacier Point Road was OPEN November 8 and 9, even though Google Maps shows it closed
• Valley roads are open all year, Highway 140, 41, and 120 west

caption:
Every Californian should drive this highway once in their life and it’s NOT Highway 1! 🛣️

This is Highway 395, the most underrated road trip in California.

It runs over 500 miles up the Eastern Sierra, and every single mile looks like a postcard: snow capped peaks, turquoise lakes, salt flats, ghost towns, and rock formations that don’t look real.

Here are the stops to make, save this for your road trip:
• Alabama Hills in Lone Pine, granite boulders with Mount Whitney towering behind them
• Mount Whitney Portal, the gateway to the tallest peak in the contiguous US
• Ancient Bristlecone Pine Forest near Big Pine, home to the oldest living trees on Earth
• Mono Lake in Lee Vining, the tufa towers rising out of the water
• Bodie Ghost Town, the best preserved ghost town in California
• June Lake Loop, the Switzerland of California
• Convict Lake, turquoise water under sheer cliffs
• Mammoth Lakes, Devils Postpile and natural hot springs

Best time to drive it: spring through fall, when all the passes are open and the lakes are blue.

• Granite arches and rounded rock formations you can walk right up to
• Movie Road, the dirt road through the most filmed spots
• Mount Whitney towering over the whole valley, the tallest peak in the contiguous US
• Golden desert light that makes every photo look like a movie still
• Zero crowds, even on weekends

Getting here: about 3.5 hours from LA, up Highway 395 to Lone Pine.

Send this to someone who is about to visit Japan because these 10 Japanese culture tips made my Japan trip 10x easier 🇯🇵

Japan runs on respect, and knowing these small rules before you go changes everything. Locals notice, and they appreciate it. Swipe through all 10, but here is the quick version:

• Politeness is everything, a small nod and a smile go a long way
• Slurping your noodles is not rude, it is encouraged
• Never stick chopsticks upright in rice, and never pass food chopstick to chopstick
• Say “Itadakimasu” before eating and “Gochisousama” after
• Trains are quiet zones, keep voices low and skip the phone calls
• Shoes come off indoors: homes, ryokan, temples, even some restaurants
• Punctuality is real, trains leave to the minute, so arrive early
• At shrines, walk to the side of the torii path and cleanse your hands first
• Respect personal space and always follow the queue

This 900 year old castle is one of the most beautiful castles in Europe and a lot of people miss it! 🏰
📍 Edinburgh Castle, Scotland

You were promised facts, so here they are 👇

Edinburgh Castle sits on top of Castle Rock, an ancient volcanic crag right in the heart of Edinburgh. Inside you will find St Margaret’s Chapel, the oldest surviving building in Edinburgh, built in the 1100s.

It is home to the Honours of Scotland, the oldest crown jewels in Britain, plus the Stone of Destiny. Every day at 1 PM (except Sundays), the One O’Clock Gun fires, a tradition running since 1861. It is also known as one of the most besieged fortresses in the world.

Tips for visiting:
• Book tickets online in advance, it sells out
• Go early morning for fewer crowds
• Walk down the Royal Mile after your visit
• Do not miss the panoramic city views from the battlements

caption:
After visiting Switzerland for 2 weeks, here are 5 MISTAKES you need to avoid 🚨🇨🇭
Details in the caption 👇

Switzerland is a dream, but it is also one of the most expensive countries in Europe 💸 These are the 5 Switzerland travel mistakes that cost us the most money, so you can avoid them on your trip ✈️

1️⃣ Not buying the Swiss Half Fare Card 🚆
Swiss trains, buses, and mountain railways are world class but pricey! The Half Fare Card costs CHF 120 and gets you 50% off most public transport. It pays for itself in days. Skip it and you will overspend big time 😅

2️⃣ Not booking stays with free breakfast 🍳
Hotels with included breakfast are a budget lifesaver ✨ Food is expensive in Switzerland, and mornings on the go get hectic. Fuel up for hikes 🥾 and start the day stress free!

3️⃣ Eating out for every meal 🍽️
Restaurant prices add up fast! Grab fresh premade meals at Migros or Coop instead 🛒 They are affordable, easy to heat, and surprisingly good 😋

4️⃣ Not using the SBB Mobile app 📱
This app is a game changer for Swiss train travel 🗺️ Real time schedules, route options, and easy ticket booking. Pro tip: you can often book your entire route including transfers for one price instead of paying per leg 💡

5️⃣ Not using travel credit cards 💳
We flew Chicago to Zurich round trip using points and perks ✈️ If you are not stacking travel credit card points, you are leaving free money on the table 💰

caption:
How much does it actually cost to visit Yellowstone + Grand Teton? 👀🏔️

We broke down every major cost so you can actually plan this trip flights, hotels, rental cars, food, gas, and park entrance fees for Yellowstone National Park and Grand Teton National Park.

For a 4–5 day trip, a realistic budget is around $1,300–$1,600 per person, depending on your travel dates, which gateway town you stay in (Jackson, West Yellowstone, or Gardiner), and how early you book flights.

Here’s where the money goes on a Yellowstone and Grand Teton road trip:
✈️ Flights: biggest variable fly into Jackson Hole or Bozeman and compare both
🏨 Hotels: book 6+ months out for summer, prices spike in June- August
🚗 Rental car: non-negotiable, the parks are huge and there’s no real transit
⛽ Gas: you’ll drive hundreds of miles between geyser basins, Old Faithful, Grand Prismatic, Jenny Lake, and Mormon Row
🎟️ Park pass: one America the Beautiful pass covers both parks for a full year

Pro tip: visiting in shoulder season (May or September) can cut your Yellowstone trip cost significantly, fewer crowds, cheaper lodging, and the wildlife is unreal.

caption:
This is the most scenic drive in South Dakota and almost no one talks about it 👇

Needles Highway is a 14 mile drive inside Custer State Park, South Dakota that winds through granite spires, one-lane rock tunnels, and hairpin turns.

It’s in the Black Hills between Custer and Mt Rushmore and it’s one of the best road trips in the USA if you love dramatic landscapes.

📍 SAVE THIS FOR YOUR BLACK HILLS TRIP:
Must stop along the drive:
Needles Eye Tunnel - one lane tunnel carved through granite
Cathedral Spires Overlook - best photo spot
Sylvan Lake for hiking & picnics
Hike if you have time:
Cathedral Spires Trail, 1.6 miles out & back to the base of granite walls
Sunday Gulch Trail, 3.9 mile loop from Sylvan Lake with ladders + scrambles
Little Devil’s Tower Trail, 3.8 miles with views of Black Elk Peak

Best time to go: Summer to early fall. Go early morning or late afternoon, less traffic, better light. Winter = road closures.

Pro tip: Drive slow, road is VERY narrow. Vehicles over 8ft wide / 12ft tall won’t fit through tunnels. Pair it with Wildlife Loop Road in Custer State Park.

caption:
Steal my Mount Rainier itinerary 🏔️ I did the research so you don’t have to

Save this if Washington is on your 2026 bucket list. This park has it all wildflower meadows, glaciers, alpine lakes, and waterfalls that don’t even look real.

My perfect 1-2 day route 👇

PARADISE SIDE (Don’t skip this)
Skyline Trail - 5.5 miles - The BEST hike in the park. 360° views of Rainier, glaciers, marmots, and endless wildflowers in late July/Aug.

Nisqually Vista Trail - 1.2 miles - All the glacier views with almost no effort.

Myrtle Falls - 1 mile - The iconic postcard view of Rainier + waterfall. Go before 9am.

SUNRISE SIDE (Best for fewer crowds)
Fremont Lookout - 5.6 miles - Fire lookout with insane ridge views. Feels like you’re on top of the PNW.

Sunrise Nature Trail - 1.5 miles - Easy meadow loop if you’re short on time.

MY FAVORITE LOOP NEAR THE PARK:
Naches Peak Loop - 3.5 miles at Tipsoo Lake - Wildflowers + perfect lake reflection of Rainier. This is THE photo spot.

Add these if you have time: Christine Falls, Narada Falls, Reflection Lakes, Bench & Snow Lakes, Silver Falls

PRO TIPS to save you time:
1.  Paradise entrance gets full by 9:30am in summer - enter early
2.  Late July to mid-Aug is peak wildflower season
3.  No timed entry needed for 2026, but parking is brutal
